ownership_changes: QrLoginService.beginAttempt/cancelAttempt define an explicit attempt with the current AuthManager session generation. start/poll/exchange accept the attempt id and check ownership at request/publication boundaries.

A superseded or cancelled exchange cannot publish tokens, set authenticated state, write an owner marker or navigate after the establishment check. An already-issued owner request may be in flight; cancellation bumps the authentication-attempt sequence so the publication predicate rejects it.

Successful exchange publishes through AuthManager.establishAuthenticatedSession with a new authentication attempt and an active-attempt predicate. AuthManager increments an authentication-attempt sequence on sign-in, TV exchange, bootstrap and sign-out so stale completions cannot overwrite a later session.

A failed establishment signs out only when the exchange still owns the current authentication attempt; otherwise it removes only the QR token pair it wrote. Email and TV exchange establishment failures use the same rule.
Cleanup invalidates the current attempt and clears an unapproved anonymous caller's tokens. Already-issued remote requests cannot be undone; the local publication boundary is what is controlled.
QR error text is redacted for the code and device nonce; console diagnostics use fixed messages.
rendering_changes: Removed the external api.qrserver.com image fallback; start() returns only an upstream qr_image_url or null.
isSafeQrImageUrl accepts same-origin HTTPS, the fixture loopback HTTP origin, or base64 image data; rejects javascript:, cross-origin, credential-bearing and quote/control-character URLs.
The screen creates the image node with document.createElement, sets src/alt as properties and uses textContent for the explicit unavailable state.
Hostile image URL test asserts no image node, no script execution, no evil-host request and zero external QR renderer requests.

When upstream omits qr_image_url, the screen uses the existing local QrCodeGenerator with the validated login URL, so the flow does not depend on a third-party renderer. The hostile-image path still rejects the hostile URL and renders the local QR instead.
browser_test_limits: Synthetic identity/add-on origins only; no live Nuvio service, QR consent or device observation.
The local QR is generated from a synthetic login URL; no real device scans it.
The held-exchange/owner tests prove no later local token/state/navigation publication; an already-issued owner request may still be in flight.
residual_risks: Tokens remain in same-origin localStorage; a same-origin script can still read them. This change does not eliminate that architecture or claim the application is XSS-proof.
Local sign-out/cleanup is not proof of remote session revocation.
Live QR approval, consent, expiry, nonce and device behavior remain blocked under #120 and are not claimed here.
